# NOTES ON THREE BOOKS (for later Q&A; text not needed)

## BOOK 1: The Young Naval Captain; or The War of All Nations (Ralph Bonehill / Edward Stratemeyer; 1902)
**Setting:** Future war, 1936+. US (incl. Canada, Cuba, PR, Philippines, Hawaii) vs world (England, France, Germany, Russia, Japan, China, Italy, Spain, Turkey). President Jefferson McKinley Adams; Secretary of Navy Short. Standard Shipyard, Bridgeport. Commodore David Pelham (deceased father of Oscar).

**Characters:** Oscar Pelham (hero, ~20, inventor, captain); Andy Greggs (machinist, first lieutenant, chum); George Dross (old engineer); Jim/Marney/Walton (ammunition man)/Gilson/Jones; Senator Forbish; Commodore Garrison; Admiral Fielding; Admiral Alvin Chester (Pacific); Commodore Gresson (British); Hang Chang (Chinese captain); Lt. Raxtell (madman); Gabretti (Italian traitor, ex-engineer who blew up Holland I); Captain Roquez (Spanish); Nathan Pargloss (corrupt ex-Treasury man); Martha Adams (President's daughter, kidnapped); Jean Fevre (French dude); Lt. Chan Lee/Chinese captains.

**Events in order:**
1. War declared (spring 1936) against the world; Oscar and Andy at Bridgeport; firm offered $50,000 bonus.
2. Holland I blown up by Gabretti; Oscar's submarine Holland XI (aluminum/steel, 115 ft, 23 knots); Secretary Short's offer; new Holland built in 30 days for $500,000.
3. Destroys Chinese cruiser Tien-Tsin at Baracoa, Cuba (electric-timed torpedo, 5 minutes).
4. Escapes French cruiser Republique's shell; buried in sand; prisoners of sea; air-supply escape; Oscar captured by Japanese, freed by Andy; dynamite bombs on Japanese column.
5. Lt. Raxtell's madness foiled; torpedoes sink German Wilhelm II, British Terrible, French Philippe (Gulf of St. Lawrence).
6. Fraudulent messenger; trap with copper netting; English despatch boat rammed.
7. Battle off Casco Bay/Portland; Virginia saved; Ivan/Coronet sunk; Turkish/Italian transports at Boston.
8. Canal (Central America); Pargloss drowns after sabotage at lock.
9. Honolulu: foreign ships blown up; tidal wave strands Holland; whales; Pacific storm.
10. Hang Chang captured; Oscar's secret code (16 = enemy here, 9 = go down).
11. Alaska/Cape Nome: Ivan II sunk (wire-alarm defenses); Hang Chang drags Oscar into sea, killed by Andy.
12. Holland captured by Spanish Captain Roquez and Gabretti; retaken; Roquez prisoner at Santiago de Cuba.
13. Caribbean earthquake/volcano; French ship Bordeaux survivor Jean Fevre.
14. Green Dragon: Martha Adams rescued; Oscar shot in shoulder; war ends. Oscar made Rear Admiral; wife Martha. Andy and George Dross commodores.

**Key facts:** Holland XI is the boat; 8.6k $ per torpedo; Oscar's medal; highite (new explosive). Congress medal. Fraud: "Mrs. Adams"/Archie Biggil not relevant here.

## BOOK 2: Footprints (Kay Cleaver Strahan; 1929)
**Setting:** Quilter family, Q 2 Ranch, Quilter County, eastern Oregon. Murder of Richard "Dick" Quilter, Monday night Oct 8, 1900; shot in left chest from ~several feet with .38 Colt; found in bed; window open; rope tied to bed leg hanging out over porch roof; newly fallen snow, no footprints.

**Family:** Thaddeus Quilter (grandfather, 80, Schiller translator, "Be generous rather than just"); Richard "Dick" (victim, father of 3, stomach cancer, planned his own death for insurance $10,000, lapsed/paid by Dr. Joe); Neal Quilter (18 then, narrator of letters, later 46; confessed then recanted; actually Grandfather told at end? Final: Dick planned, Grandfather helped? Ending reveals Dr. Joe confessed he killed Dick at Dick's request; Dr. Joe was in Portland); Judith "Judy" Quilter Whitefield (eldest daughter, in Colorado, husband Greg); Lucy Quilter (12, letter writer, later famous author, married Cerini); Gracia "Aunt Gracia" (Dick's sister, Siloamite convert, mystic); Phineas (uncle, prospector, Olympe's husband, "Pan"); Olympe (actress wife of Phineas); Christopher "Chris" (cousin, playwright, handsome; wife Irene, formerly Mrs. Biggil, "Booful"); Irene (chatterbox, locked doors, first husband Archie Biggil); Dr. Joseph "Dr. Joe" Elm (family doctor, ~pink baldness, Portland); Dong Lee (Chinese house boy); Neal's "Ursula Thornton" (later love).
**Investigation:** Coroner Hank Buckerman; Gus Wildoch (sheriff); Benjamin Thopson (DA's man); Bruno Ward (Portland lawyer); Mattie Blaine (stenographer); jury incl. Roy Ulander, John Skrope, George Houndel, Pete Garret.
**Crime analyst:** Lynn MacDonald (SF, red hair, gray eyes); Dr. Joe hired her, read letters; Dr. Joe confessed; Lynn's theory: Dick planned death; Dr. Joe shot him at Dick's request; "footprints on sands of time".
**Ending:** Dr. Joe says "I killed Dick… I did it for Dick"; Neal forgets/has amnesia; Judith hears; Neal's realization that Grandfather "would be the one who would cover it up." Final: Neal's letters are in Lynn's file.

## BOOK 3: The Pillar of Light (Louis Tracy; 1904)
**Setting:** Gulf Rock lighthouse, off Cornwall (Penzance, Scilly Isles). Stephen Brand (assistant-keeper, 50, ex-attaché; ninth baronet of Lesser Hambledon, Northumberland). Adopted/house: daughter Constance Brand (19, brown hair, hazel eyes); foundling Enid Trevillion (19, flaxen hair, blue eyes; found June 1885/1886 in boat, marked "E.T.", emerald shamrock brooch).
**Other characters:** Jim Spence (lame ex-navy assistant-keeper), Jones (head-keeper, sciatica), Thompson, Bates (broken leg), Jackson (scalded), Ben Pollard (fisherman, boat *Daisy*), Lt. John Percival "Jack" Stanhope RN (Enid's suitor; mother Lady Margaret Stanhope), Charles A. Pyne (American, nephew of Cyrus J. Traill, Philadelphian millionaire; climbed foremast), Nanette "Mrs. Vansittart" (Brand's wife, Madeleine Nanette de Courtray; eloped; formerly Mrs. Brand), Mr. Emmett (chief officer of *Chinook*), Mrs. Sheppard (nurse/housekeeper), Elsie and Mamie (orphan children), Mrs. Taylor, Mrs. Taylor-Smith.
**Ship:** *Chinook* (formerly *Princess Royal*, Southampton-New York liner; capt. Perkins) wrecked on Gulf Rock during hurricane.
**Events in order:**
1. June 1885: Brand (keeper) kills shark, rescues infant (E.T.) from boat; named Enid after Arthurian "Enid the Good", surname Trevillion.
2. Jan 1904 (morning): Stanhope aboard *Princess Royal* near Gulf Rock; Enid and Constance sail *Daisy* with Ben Pollard to rock; storm; rocket signals; Jackson and Bates hurt, lowered in boat.
3. Girls remain on rock; hurricane; Brand fears collapse; cocoa; wave hits lantern.
4. *Chinook* wrecked on reef (captain drowned with ship); Pyne climbs foremast with rope; ~78 survivors crowd lighthouse.
5. Brand distributes stores; mutiny/drunkenness (methylated spirit); rain catch.
6. Brand's shelter plans; Mrs. Vansittart's identity; Brand's wife.
7. Raft attempt fails; Stanhope rows boat with Ben Pollard and Jim Spence; Brand pours colza oil on sea; Stanhope's rope; rescue.
8. Traill's letter: Enid is his daughter Edith (lost in *Esmeralda* 1885).
9. Mrs. Vansittart confesses; she flees; Brand reunited with wife; she leaves; Brand says "Nanette"; they reconcile and remarry.
10. Ending: marriages — Enid to Stanhope; Constance to Pyne; Brand & Nanette remarried; voyage to Far West.

**Key details:** Light: occulting then fixed; 130 ft, 8-wick dioptric lens; 3,000 gallons colza oil; storm-shutters; auriscope (Brand's sound-detector invention); Marconi not present.
